title: Asteria Capital private deploy intake notes
content:
Context:
- First intake call with Asteria Capital (quant trading platform) on 2024-11-29. They want an on-prem / VPC-private deployment for market-sensitive prompt routing and model inference of their risk-analysis assistant.
- Primary ask: low-latency (<60ms p50 for 256-token sequences) production inference with deterministic isolation and KMS-backed key control. 6-month pilot, then evaluate Dedicated vs Private for full rollout.

Call notes (rough):
- Attendees: Daniel Park (Asteria CTO), Sienna Cho (Head of ML infra), Raj Patel (SecOps), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Jonah Liu (Redwood infra eng)
- They run on-prem colos (Equinix) and have a hybrid cloud policy. No external internet egress from model subnet allowed by default.
- Data classification: prompts can contain PII + market positions. Must remain in customer VPC; audit logs must be delivered to their SIEM (SumoLogic) and to their internal Kafka for retention.
- Throughput target: steady 750 qps concurrent small requests (average 64 tokens) during market open bursts.
- Budget: pilot cap ~$40k/mo (hardware + Redwood support) but willing to increase for clear perf wins.

Technical constraints / implications:
- Network: need private endpoint; control-plane comms must either be via a dedicated control-plane VPN or a self-hosted control plane. They prefer self-hosted control plane option.
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with their Thales Luna HSM for both model encryption keys and signing of audit logs. Redwood supports KMS integration but HSM flow needs ops runbook and IAM mapping.
- No outbound calls from serving nodes to public model hubs. We need to plan for model artifact transfer via customer-approved staging bucket or air-gapped transfer.
- Compliance: want FIPS-ish crypto, SOC2 mapped controls, and full audit trail with immutable event IDs.

Serving/runtime specifics discussed:
- Model: they want to run a tuned Llama-3-70B variant (quantized to 4-bit). Need to validate perf on their GPUs (A100 40GB / H100?).
- KV cache persistence: they want ephemeral caches per-request but are open to prefix caching for repeated queries. We need to propose cache TTLs and eviction to balance cost/latency.
- Batching: workload is bursty during market close; recommend adaptive batching + token-aware batching.
- Canary/fallback policy: need a policy to fallback to a smaller quantized model if peak latency breaches SLOs.

Immediate gotchas / risks:
- HSM integration may add multi-week ops work — include as a risk in pilot deck. If HSM cannot sign logs, they may accept KMS but require extra compensating controls.
- Their no-egress rule blocks our normal hosted artifact fetch; offline transfer process needs confirmation.
- GPU memory: Llama-3-70B even quantized could exceed single 40GB A100 unless shard+nvlink used. Need profiling run.
- Telemetry: they insist on sending logs to their Kafka; ensure log format/payload size acceptable and PII redaction configurable.

Metrics / SLOs to confirm:
- Latency: p50 <60ms, p95 <200ms for 256-token sequences (make sure we clarify tokenization baseline).
- Availability: 99.9% per month (pilot SLA to be negotiated).
- Cost per 1M tokens (estimate) to be provided by Redwood Infra team based on profiling.

Action items / next steps (owner / ETA):
- Jonah: Schedule micro-benchmark run of quantized Llama-3-70B on Asteria sample host (need access window) — target 2024-12-10.
- Priya: Draft pilot statement of work (SOW) and risk log; include HSM fallback and offline artifact flow — draft due 2024-12-06.
- Marisol: Prepare compliance checklist mapping Redwood Private features to their SOC2/FIPS needs; include audit log format sample — 2024-12-08.
- Daniel (Asteria): Confirm available GPU hardware spec (exact A100/H100 submodel + nvlink config) and provide firewall/VPN contacts for control-plane options — 2024-12-05.
- Raj (Asteria SecOps): Share Thales HSM admin contact and initial policy (key rotation, signing modules) — 2024-12-04.

Notes to self / SE playbook fragments:
- If HSM signing is blocker, propose two-stage approach: (1) pilot with envelope encryption using their KMS (software-backed) + hardened access controls, (2) parallel integration with HSM in week 4-6.
- Offline model import checklist: artifact checksum (sha256), signed manifest, approved operator account, transfer via SFTP into staging bucket, validation job run by Redwood infra.
- Default telemetry plan: ship compact events to their Kafka with an opt-in full payload for incidents. Avoid sending raw prompts to external endpoints.

Open questions (need answers before SOW finalization):
- Can Asteria accept a temporary bastion host that has outbound egress only for artifact polling? (If no, we need manual transfer cadence).
- Do they require FIPS 140-2 level 3 HSM certification for sign/crypt ops or will level 2 suffice for pilot?
- What retention window for audit logs (30d, 90d, custom)? Impacts storage/retention cost.
- Are they open to a hybrid control-plane (Redwood-managed but on VPC peered with customer) as intermediate step?

Loose timeline idea:
- Week 0: access agreements + NDA extension for on-prem work
- Week 1-2: infra profiling + initial bench runs
- Week 3: pilot SOW signed; build baseline config (network, KMS proof-of-concept)
- Week 4-8: pilot run with canary traffic and regression checks

Draft subject line for customer email: "Redwood — Asteria Capital private deployment pilot proposal + next steps"

Random scribbles / fragments captured in call:
- "We need deterministic token accounting for billing — also need to ensure no hidden cache duplicates"
- "If we can't use HSM we'll need a signed attestation flow"
- TODO: check model license for Llama-3-70B variant and commercial use limits (ask Product/Legal).

Reference links (internal):
- Private deploy quickstart playbook: confluence:Private-Deploy-Quickstart
- HSM integration notes: GH:infra/hsm-integration-notes.md
- Offline artifact transfer runbook: confluence:Offline-Artifact-Transfers
